content: VIT (Latin vita, life) means life; the verb
vivere, to live, gives VIV. MORT (Latin
mors, mortis, death) means death.
vital     of life
revive    again + live
immortal  not + subject to death
mortify   to make dead
A mortgage is a dead pledge: mort + gage,
a pledge that dies when the debt is paid.
To mortify is to kill the pride.
Morbid is a near neighbor, not the same
word: morbus, disease.
THE NEXT 16 CARDS: vit, viv and mort words.
SENT (Latin sentire, to feel) means feel.
TANG (Latin tangere, to touch) means touch;
its past form tactus gives TACT.
consent   together + feel
dissent   apart + feel
tangible  able to be touched
intact    not + touched
Intact is the quiet one: not touched, and
therefore whole. A tangent touches a curve
once and leaves, which is what a tangential
remark does.
Tact is the same touch, refined into a feel
for what is fitting.
THE NEXT 16 CARDS: sent and tang words.
GREG (Latin grex, gregis, flock) means
flock. JUNCT (Latin jungere, to join)
means join.
congregate   together + flock
segregate    apart + flock
junction     a joining
conjunction  together + joining
Egregious once meant out of the flock and
so remarkable. It now means remarkably bad,
and nothing else.
Subjugate, conjugate and jugular carry
jugum, the yoke that joins two oxen.
THE NEXT 15 CARDS: greg and junct words.
TERR (Latin terra, land) means land, earth.
HAB (Latin habere, to have) means have,
hold; after a prefix it becomes HIB.
territory     place of land
subterranean  under + earth
prohibit      before + hold
exhibit       out + hold
The verb inter, to bury, is in + terra: to
put into the earth. It is not the prefix
inter-, between.
Habitare, to dwell, gives habitat and
inhabit. Debt is the far one: debitum,
that which is held from another.
THE NEXT 19 CARDS: terr and hab words.
LEG has two Latin parents: lex, legis, law,
and legere, to read or to choose. NOMEN
(Latin nomen, nominis) means name.
legal     of the law
elect     out + chosen
lecture   a reading
nominate  to name
Legal and legislate come from lex. Elect,
select, collect, neglect and eligible come
from legere. A legend is legenda, the thing
to be read.
Anonymous is the Greek twin of nomen:
onoma, the same name in another alphabet.
THE NEXT 18 CARDS: leg and nomen words.
PLIC (Latin plicare, to fold) means fold.
It wears many coats: PLEX, PLY, PLOY, PLI.
explicit   out + folded
implicit   in + folded
complex    together + folded
duplicate  two + folded
The root is doing harder work now. It no
longer folds cloth; it folds meaning.
Explicit is laid open, implicit is folded
in, an accomplice is folded in with you.
Reply, supply, employ and deploy came
through French with the fold worn down to
ply and ploy.
THE NEXT 21 CARDS: plic words.
